ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a leaf-like structure of a fern plant, with pinnate leaflets in the center and a stalk extending downward. On the right side there is a longest bracket, covering the complete length from the top leaf tip to the lower base of the stalk, indicating the entire visible structure. Reasoning: The question asks what the “complete length” of this structure is called, not a certain leaflet or local part. In fern plants, the whole leaf including the blade part and the petiole is called frond.
